issue: The cooling-off rule is stated with the wrong measuring point. The key takeaway says a former engagement-team member 'cannot become CEO, CFO, controller, or chief accounting officer ... within one year before the audit period begins'. The worked example says the firm is not independent 'unless a full year separates her last audit work from the start of that audit period'. In SEC terms, the 'audit period' is the period covered by the financial statements (Rule 2-01(f)(5)(i)), so it starts on the first day of the fiscal year. The rule actually looks back one year from the start of audit procedures for the fiscal period that includes the hire date. As written, the takeaway is garbled: it restricts when the person becomes CFO instead of when the person last took part in the audit. It also gives no measuring point that would let a student work the scenario items.
evidence: SOX §206 and Rule 2-01(c)(2)(iii)(B): the firm is not independent if a former audit engagement team member (the lead or concurring partner, or anyone else with more than 10 hours of audit services) holds a financial reporting oversight role (FROR), unless that person did not take part in the audit during the one-year period before audit procedures began for the fiscal period that includes the date they were first employed. The SEC treats audit procedures as beginning the day after the prior year's 10-K is filed, so in practice one full audit cycle must pass. Counter-example to the lesson's anchor: calendar-year issuer, FY2026 audit period begins Jan 1, 2026, and FY2026 audit procedures begin Mar 1, 2026, the day after the FY2025 10-K is filed. A manager whose last audit work was Feb 20, 2026 joins as CFO in Nov 2026. Measured against the 'audit period' start (Jan 1, 2026), her last work is not within the year before it. Measured against the start of procedures (Mar 1, 2026), she took part during the preceding year, so the firm is impaired. The items take the rule's view: aud-spi-03 says 'the audit of the following year begins four months after her last work'. The reference sheet (aud-standards.md §5) also says the year is measured 'from the start of the current audit'.
source: SOX §206; SEC Rule 2-01(c)(2)(iii)(B) and 2-01(f)(5); SEC Release 33-8183 (2003). Search summary: https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/sec/sec_faqs/sec_faqs_US/auditor_independence_US/C-Employment-relationships.html ; https://www.paulweiss.com/media/2366141/audind2-18-03.pdf
fix: Rewrite the takeaway: 'Cooling-off: the firm is not independent if a former audit engagement team member (lead or concurring partner, or anyone with more than 10 audit hours) is in a financial reporting oversight role at the issuer (e.g., CEO, CFO, controller, CAO), unless the person did not take part in the audit during the one year before the current audit began. In practice, a full audit cycle must pass.' In the worked example, replace 'from the start of that audit period' with 'from the start of the audit procedures for the year she joins'.

issue: The skill labels on four items are two or more levels too high, and their difficulty labels are inflated as well. aud-spi-24 (analysis, difficulty 3) asks what permitted tax services require; the answer, 'committee pre-approval', is pure recall. aud-spi-25 (analysis, difficulty 3) is the partner-compensation rule in a one-line stem; that is recall. aud-spi-26 (evaluation, difficulty 3) applies the one-year cooling-off rule; that is application at most. aud-spi-27 (evaluation, difficulty 3) asks about a contingent fee for tax planning; that is recall. All four are among the easiest items in the module: one-line stems, with distractors such as 'No effect' and 'Nothing'.
evidence: Compare same-fact items that carry lower labels: aud-spi-14 (contingent fee, analysis) and aud-spi-27 (evaluation); aud-spi-03 (cooling-off scenario, application) and aud-spi-26 (evaluation); aud-x1-08 (pre-approval, remembering, difficulty 1) and aud-spi-24 (analysis, difficulty 3). Under the Blueprint's definitions, evaluation means examining or assessing problems and using professional judgment to draw conclusions. None of these items calls for that. The mislabels push the module's analysis and evaluation counts (4 and 2 by cues.md) above what the items actually test, which distorts the AUD skill-mix tracking (analysis 15–25%, evaluation 5–15%).
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/aud.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel: aud-spi-24 to remembering, difficulty 1; aud-spi-25 to remembering, difficulty 1; aud-spi-26 to application, difficulty 2; aud-spi-27 to remembering, difficulty 1. Alternatively, rewrite them as real multi-fact scenarios that justify the higher levels.

issue: The skill labels on seven items are one level too high. Five pure-recall questions are labeled application: aud-spi-12 (pre-approval through detailed policies), aud-spi-16 (lead partner, 5 years), aud-spi-17 (SOX §407), aud-spi-18 (404(b) exemption) and aud-spi-20 (Form AP). Two single-fact scenarios are labeled analysis when they are application: aud-spi-14 (contingent tax fee) and aud-spi-19 (partner compensation).
evidence: aud-spi-16 has almost the same stem as aud-spi-chk2 and aud-spi-21 (Jaccard 0.83 and 0.75), and both of those are labeled remembering. aud-spi-17, -18 and -20 ask 'What does X require' or 'Which issuers are exempt', with no fact pattern to apply. aud-spi-14 and -19 each turn on recognizing one prohibited arrangement, which fits the Blueprint's application level.
fix: Relabel aud-spi-12, -16, -17, -18 and -20 as remembering, and aud-spi-14 and -19 as application.

issue: The practice pool contains four near-identical pairs that test the same fact in the same way: 02/13 (preparing the CFO's personal tax return, Rule 3523); 14/27 (a contingent fee for tax planning); 16/21 (the lead partner's 5-year limit); 19/25 (partner pay for selling non-audit services). Lead-partner rotation is tested a further two times (aud-spi-chk2 and aud-x1-20, plus TBS m1 and flashcard f3). That is six or more items on one number.
evidence: Stems: 02 'asked to prepare the personal income tax return of the company's CFO' and 13 'prepares the personal tax return of the issuer's CFO'. 14 'fee for tax planning advice that depends on the tax savings' and 27 'contingent fee for tax planning'. 16 and 21 both ask 'How long may the lead ... partner serve ... before rotating off' (cues.md Jaccard 0.75). 19 'compensation depends on selling non-audit services' and 25 'paid for selling non-audit services'. Each pair has the same key concept and the same kind of distractors.
fix: Drop one item from each pair, or rewrite the second one to test an untested rule: for example, the de minimis pre-approval exception, PCAOB Rule 3525 pre-approval of ICFR-related services, an immediate family member in a FROR, the Rule 3523 exception for directors, or the rotation rule for a partner on a significant subsidiary.

issue: These items have weak or implausible distractors and answer cues. In aud-spi-13 the stem names Rule 3523 and already says the CFO is 'a person in a financial reporting oversight role', which gives the answer away; the key, 'Impaired', is also the shortest option. In aud-spi-24, 'Approval from the SEC staff' and 'Nothing' are not plausible. In aud-spi-25, 'No effect', 'Allowed if disclosed' and 'Allowed for tax services' are all bare negations. In aud-spi-26, the stem asks 'Is the firm independent?' and (d) answers 'Only if the manager was junior'. That does not fit the question grammatically and contradicts the rule's own coverage. In aud-spi-27, 'No effect' and 'Allowed if small' are throwaways.
evidence: A candidate who knows only that the rules are strict can eliminate two of the three distractors in 24, 25 and 27. In 13 the answer is in the stem. In 26, (d) neither answers yes nor no, and the 'junior' qualifier has no basis in any rule.
fix: In aud-spi-13, remove 'Under PCAOB Rule 3523' and the FROR description from the stem, and use parallel option lengths. Replace the throwaway options with misconceptions candidates actually hold: for example, 'Permitted because the fee is below 5% of total fees (de minimis)', 'Permitted if the audit committee approves it in advance' or 'Permitted for tax services only'. Rewrite 26(d) as 'Yes, because a manager is not a partner'.

issue: Several explanations are thin or circular and teach nothing. aud-spi-22 gives 'That is not the rule.' for all three distractors, without saying that 2 years is the other-partner time-out and 5 years the lead-partner time-out. In aud-spi-21, (c) and (d) say only 'That period is too short/long.' aud-spi-24, -25 and -27 give 'It's prohibited.', 'That is not allowed.' and 'That is not required.' The overall explanation for aud-x1-08 is just 'SOX Section 202.'
evidence: Compare aud-spi-03 and aud-spi-08, whose distractor explanations name the rule each wrong number comes from: 'Five years is the partner rotation time-out, not the cooling-off period.'
fix: Rewrite each distractor explanation to name the rule it confuses. For example, 22(a): '2 years is the time-out for other audit partners after 7 years.' 27(c): 'Rule 3521 has no size exception; any contingent fee impairs independence.' Expand the aud-x1-08 explanation: 'SOX §202 (Exchange Act §10A(i)): the audit committee pre-approves all audit and permitted nonaudit services, either specifically or through detailed policies; it may delegate to a member but never to management.'

issue: The stem measures the wrong interval, and the explanation does not teach the right one. The stem says the manager 'becomes the issuer's CFO 8 months after the last audit's start'. The cooling-off test turns on whether the person took part in the audit during the one year before the current audit began. The stem gives neither the date of her last audit work nor the start of the current audit. The explanation, 'The 1-year cooling-off isn't met', implies the year runs from the last audit's start to the hire date. That reinforces the mismeasurement that the lesson finding also flags.
evidence: Under typical annual cycles, a manager on an audit that began 8 months before the hire date almost certainly worked on the audit within the one year before the next audit began, so the key (c) holds. The reasoning the item models is still wrong. Suppose the manager left that engagement early, more than a year before the current audit began: the firm would then be independent, and the stem cannot rule that out.
fix: Restate it with dates. For example: 'A manager's last work on Ivy Corp.'s 20X4 audit was on Feb 25, 20X5. Audit procedures for 20X5 began Mar 1, 20X5, and she became Ivy's CFO on Nov 1, 20X5. Is the firm independent for the 20X5 audit?' Key: No; she took part in the audit during the one year before the 20X5 audit began. Explain the look-back in the explanation.

issue: Eight practice items test material the lesson never teaches. The lesson does not cover: SOX §301 audit committee responsibility for the auditor (aud-spi-11); how pre-approval may be given, either specifically or through detailed policies with no delegation to management (aud-spi-12); PCAOB inspection frequency (aud-spi-15); SOX §407 (aud-spi-17); the 404(b) exemption (aud-spi-18); the ban on partner pay for selling non-audit services under Rule 2-01(c)(8) (aud-spi-19 and -25); and Form AP (aud-spi-20). A grep of all content found no lesson that teaches Form AP or the partner-compensation rule. Section 404(b) and §407 are taught only in aud-understanding-entity (aud-u4), and the 3-year inspection cycle only in aud-quality-management (aud-u2). Both modules come later in the sequence.
evidence: Searched the lesson body and takeaways for: 301, 407, 404, inspect, Form AP, compensation, 'detailed policies'. None are present. Grep of content/ for 'Form AP' and 'selling non-audit' found only this module's questions.json. aud-understanding-entity/lesson.md:121–122 teaches §404(b) and §407.
fix: Add a short 'Audit committee and SOX governance' section. It should cover SOX §301; SOX §202 pre-approval, specific or through detailed policies, delegable to a committee member and never to management, with the de minimis exception; the Rule 2-01(c)(8) partner-compensation rule; and Form AP. Alternatively, move aud-spi-15, -17 and -18 to the modules that teach them, or mark them as cross-module.

issue: The DOL summary is incomplete and conflicts with the other module that covers it. The lesson limits trustee, officer and employee impairments to 'during the engagement period'. 29 CFR 2509.75-9 applies the tests during the period of professional engagement, at the date of the opinion, and during the period covered by the financial statements. The lesson also leaves out the DOL rule that a firm which maintains the plan's financial records is not independent; this is a key point where DOL is stricter than the AICPA Code. It also leaves out the promoter, underwriter and investment-adviser roles. aud-government-compliance/lesson.md:37 states the rule as 'during the engagement or the period covered', so the platform states the rule two different ways.
evidence: Lesson line ~126: 'serving as a trustee, officer, or employee of the plan or sponsor during the engagement period'. Reference sheet §8 (29 CFR 2509.75-9): '...at any time during the engagement, at the opinion date, or during the period covered by the FS ... maintained the plan's financial records'. aud-government-compliance lesson: '...during the engagement or the period covered'. REVIEW.md had already flagged the DOL summary for a second check.
fix: Rewrite the bullet: 'An accountant is not independent if, during the period of professional engagement, at the date of the opinion, or during the period covered by the financial statements, the accountant or firm: has a direct or material indirect financial interest in the plan or sponsor; is connected as a promoter, underwriter, investment adviser, voting trustee, director, officer or employee of the plan or sponsor; or maintains the plan's financial records. Bookkeeping is therefore stricter than under the AICPA Code.'

issue: The lesson cites PCAOB Rules 3520–3526 but never mentions Rule 3525, which requires specific pre-approval of non-audit services related to internal control over financial reporting (ICFR). Its 'permitted' list also includes 'reviews of internal control', a phrase that is not a defined service category.
evidence: Reference sheet §5: 'Rule 3525 covers pre-approval of non-audit services related to ICFR.' The lesson's PCAOB section lists 3521, 3522, 3523, 3524 and 3526 only.
fix: Add the bullet: 'Rule 3525: before the audit committee pre-approves a non-audit service related to ICFR, the auditor describes it in writing, discusses its effect on independence, and documents the discussion.' Replace 'reviews of internal control' with 'internal-control-related services (Rule 3525)'.

issue: The lesson and items leave out the SEC rules on financial, employment and business relationships under Rule 2-01(c)(1)–(3). These include the 2019 loan-provision change from a 10% bright-line test to significant influence, and the rule that a close family member in a FROR impairs independence. The module covers only nonaudit services, fees, rotation and cooling-off. All GAO and DOL items in this module (aud-spi-06, aud-spi-07, aud-x1-09) are recall-level, although the Blueprint expects candidates to apply these rules to situations. Some application coverage exists in aud-government-compliance (for example, aud-gov-07).
evidence: Lesson headings: Why issuers are different; Prohibited nonaudit services; PCAOB tax-service limits; Rotation and cooling-off; GAO; DOL. Nothing covers SEC financial interests, loans or family relationships, even though the reference sheet (§5) records the 2019 and 2020 SEC amendments. The skill labels on the GAO and DOL items are all 'remembering'.
source: SEC Rule 2-01(c)(1)–(3) (as amended 2019 and 2020); AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint Area I (SEC/PCAOB and GAO/DOL independence tasks)
fix: Add a short section comparing SEC and AICPA rules on investments, loans (the significant-influence test), and immediate and close family in FROR or accounting roles. Add two or three application items on these, and one application-level scenario each for GAGAS and DOL. Example: a firm that keeps a plan's books cannot audit it under DOL rules.

issue: The key in aud-x1-09 ('Confirm management's SKE and document the threat evaluation') relies on the acronym 'SKE', which the lesson never introduces. The lesson writes out 'suitable skill, knowledge, or experience' only. The explanation for aud-spi-06 (d) also uses 'SKE' without defining it. A student who learned the phrase may not recognize the acronym, and the key is also the only option that uses technical shorthand.
evidence: Lesson GAO bullets: '...confirm management has suitable skill, knowledge, or experience'. 'SKE' does not appear anywhere in lesson.md.
source: GAO Government Auditing Standards (2024 revision), ch. 3: nonaudit services requirements
fix: Spell it out in the option: 'Determine that management has suitable skill, knowledge, or experience to oversee the service, and document the evaluation.' Alternatively, introduce the 'SKE' acronym in the lesson.

issue: Trap labels do not match the misconception the distractor models. 'partial-computation' is used on items with no computation: chk2(c) '5 years on, 2 years off' mixes the lead and other-partner rules, so it is wrong-classification. 02(d) 'Permitted, if the return has no aggressive positions' applies the Rule 3522 test in place of Rule 3523, so it is wrong-rule. 19(d) 'No effect if the services are allowed' is wrong-rule. x1-28(a), the capital-repayment option, is wrong-rule or irrelevant-fact. 13(d) 'Impaired only if the return is aggressive' is labeled overgeneralization, but it narrows the rule, so it is wrong-rule.
evidence: Schema TRAP_TYPES includes wrong-rule and wrong-classification. 'partial-computation' describes a stopped-short calculation, and none of these items involves arithmetic.
fix: Relabel: chk2(c) to wrong-classification; 02(d), 13(d) and 19(d) to wrong-rule; x1-28(a) to wrong-rule.

issue: Distractor (a) is garbled: 'The person repays any capital owed by the firm within 30 days.' The firm owes a capital balance to the former partner, not the other way round. The 30-day window is invented. The real rule, Rule 2-01(c)(2)(iii)(A), requires that the person have no capital balance in the firm and no financial arrangement other than fixed payments. That is an additional condition, not an alternative to cooling-off.
evidence: Rule 2-01(c)(2)(iii)(A)(2)–(3): no capital balances; no financial arrangement other than regular payment of a fixed dollar amount not dependent on firm revenues.
fix: Reword (a) as 'The firm fully pays out the person's capital balance before the hire', and have the explanation say this is required in addition to the cooling-off period, not in place of it.

issue: In part svc, all seven rows share a two-option dropdown (Prohibited, or Permitted with pre-approval), so a guess scores 50% per row, and the part cannot test the common misconception that some services need no pre-approval. The 20-minute estimate is generous for 11 binary or three-way cells with no research or computation. Everything else checks out: all seven svc rows and the four memo answers (m1 rotate 5 years; m2 may continue 2 more years; m3 original correct; m4 audit committee) are correct, the exhibits are complete, and an untouched m3 scores correctly.
evidence: Recomputed: r1 and r4 are permitted with pre-approval; r2, r3, r5, r6 and r7 are prohibited (Rule 2-01(c)(4)(iii), (v), (ii) and (x); PCAOB Rule 3523). Memo: Ames 5/5 means rotate 5 years; Brooks (EQR) has served 3 of 5; Cho 7/2. tbsScoring.ts treats an untouched segment as its original wording, so m3 scores correct.
fix: Add a third option, 'Permitted without pre-approval', or a fourth row type for an AICPA-only distinction. Reduce minutes to about 12–15, or add a research part (for example, cite PCAOB Rule 3523 or Rule 2-01(c)(6)) to justify 20.

issue: Flashcard f2 packs a 10-item list onto one card, so it is not atomic and is hard to grade in spaced repetition. It also shortens two categories: it omits fairness opinions and contribution-in-kind reports from appraisal and valuation, and investment banking from broker-dealer and investment adviser services.
evidence: Back of f2: 'Bookkeeping; FIS design/implementation; appraisal and valuation; ... broker-dealer and investment adviser services; legal; expert services unrelated to the audit.' Reference sheet §5 lists 'appraisal or valuation services, fairness opinions and contribution-in-kind reports' and 'broker-dealer, investment adviser or investment banking services'.
fix: Split it into two or three cards grouped by the threat involved (self-review, management, advocacy), or add a mnemonic. Restore the full category names.
